_doc: Walk-the-house checklist, generated from criteria/. Designed for a phone screen while standing in a house. Regenerate when criteria change. Progress is saved per-home in the browser.

sections.title: Foundation & structure
sections.intro: The big one in Colorado Springs. Expansive clay soil moves foundations. Give this 10 real minutes.

items.text: Walk the full exterior perimeter. Any stair-step cracks in foundation or brick, especially at corners?
Drop a marble or a ball in each level. Does it roll? Which direction?
Open and close every interior door. Any sticking, or gaps that taper?
Look above every door and window frame for cracks radiating diagonally.
In the basement: cracks in the slab, especially under interior walls? Any heave?
Any sign of prior repair — piers, wall anchors, patched cracks, fresh paint on one wall only?
ASK: Has a structural engineer ever looked at this house? Any soils report?

sections.title: Roof & hail
sections.intro: Roofs are consumables here. Insurance carriers already know it.

items.text: ASK: Roof age, and is there a permit for the replacement?
ASK: Class 4 impact-resistant shingles? (Real premium discount if yes.)
Check gutters, downspouts, vents, and flashing for hail dents — soft metal tells the truth even when shingles look fine.
Look at the AC condenser fins for hail bruising.
From the ground, look for more than one shingle layer at the edges.
ASK: Any hail claims — paid or denied? Which carrier? What's the wind/hail deductible specifically?

sections.title: Drainage & grading
sections.intro: Nearly every foundation problem here starts as a water problem. Check this right after the foundation.

items.text: Does the ground slope AWAY from the house on all four sides?
Do downspouts discharge well clear of the foundation, or dump at the wall?
Do window wells have drains? Any staining showing they've held water?
Is an uphill neighbor's water routed toward this lot?
Are sprinkler heads spraying the foundation or siding?
Any large trees within ~15 ft of the foundation?

sections.title: Systems — the 1970s–80s cluster
sections.intro: Our budget lands in this era. These specific items can make a house uninsurable.

items.text: Open the electrical panel. Brand? Federal Pacific or Zinsco = full replacement.
Aluminum branch wiring? (Look for stamped ALUMINUM on cable jackets. ~1965–75 builds.)
Supply pipe material — gray or blue plastic is polybutylene, often uninsurable.
Amp service — 100A at capacity, or 200A?
Furnace and water heater age — read the labels, photograph them.
Water pressure — run an upstairs shower and flush a toilet at the same time.
ASK: Sewer lateral material and age. Scope it regardless — pre-1980 clay and cast iron fail.

sections.title: Radon
sections.intro: El Paso County is EPA Zone 1 — highest tier. Elevated readings are normal here, and basements are where bedrooms go.

items.text: Is there a mitigation system? (Sealed sump, vent pipe, inline fan running to the roof.)
ASK: Has it been tested? What was the number?
If mitigated, ASK for the post-mitigation test result.

sections.title: Wildfire & insurance
sections.intro: Waldo Canyon burned into Mountain Shadows in 2012 — inside our radius. An uninsurable house is an unbuyable house.

items.text: How close is the foothills interface and continuous vegetation?
Is there defensible space, or shrubs right against the siding?
Deck and roof materials — combustible or not?
How many ways out of the neighborhood?
DO THIS BEFORE THE INSPECTION DEADLINE: get a real insurance quote for this address.

sections.title: Layout & fit
sections.intro: 4 bed / 3 bath is the hard minimum. This section is about whether it actually works.

items.text: Count 4 real bedrooms. Does any basement bedroom have a proper egress window?
Are all 3 baths usefully placed, or is one stranded?
Where do bedrooms sit relative to each other across levels?
Is there room to host people?
Storage — closets, garage, basement.
Cell signal — check your bars in the basement and back bedrooms.

sections.title: Location & the daily reality
sections.intro: Drive time is already filtered to 10 minutes. This is about living there.

items.text: Stand outside and just listen for a minute. Arterial or highway noise?
Which way does the driveway face? North-facing holds ice for weeks — a real daily issue, worse on a slope.
Which rooms get afternoon west sun? At altitude that's brutal in summer.
Backyard privacy and sight lines from neighbors.
Mountain views — and could a future build take them?
Drive the actual route to YWAM at the hour you'd really drive it.

sections.title: Money questions
sections.intro: Under $600k is the ceiling. Protect the repair reserve.

items.text: ASK: 12 months of Colorado Springs Utilities bills — all four services on one bill, so it's a clean read on efficiency.
ASK: Is there a metro district? These add to the mill levy and are NOT an HOA, so they hide easily.
ASK: HOA dues, reserve health, and any pending special assessment.
Current property tax and mill levy for this exact parcel.
City water/sewer, or well and septic? (More likely at the Cedar Heights / Woodmen Valley edges.)
Add up what this house needs — roof, sewer, radon, drainage — before deciding the offer.
